title: World Modeling in Transformers
content:
Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence
  [Submitted on 18 Sep 2026]
    Title:World Modeling in Transformers
View PDF HTML (experimental)
            Abstract:Behavioral failures can make a transformer appear to lack a world model even when it has learned faithful representations of its environment. We demonstrate this in TaxiGPT, a transformer trained on random walks through Manhattan whose failures have been interpreted as evidence of an incoherent internal map. Through mechanistic analysis and causal interventions, we show that the model represents intersections and streets, tracks its position, and uses a goal compass to navigate. We trace its failures to interference between superposed intersection features, which disrupts localization within the internal map. Affordance packing, which groups representations of intersections with the same legal moves, helps limit the consequences of these errors. Finally, we propose mechanistic indicators that we use to compare models and show that world-modeling capacities emerge at different stages of training. Our findings motivate a shift from asking whether a model has a world model to mechanistically studying its world modeling: the interacting capacities through which it represents its environment and uses those representations to guide behavior.

report.summary: Mechanistic analysis of TaxiGPT shows transformers can learn world models, but behavioral failures arise from feature interference rather than missing internal maps.
report.background: The question of whether transformers truly learn world models is central to AI agents, robotics, self-driving, and planning systems. Prior work often judged models by behavior: if an agent gets lost or makes bad moves, researchers inferred its internal map was incoherent. TaxiGPT, trained on random walks through Manhattan, became a key example because its navigation failures looked like evidence against world modeling. However, behavioral failure can have many causes, including representational interference, optimization quirks, or training stage effects. This paper applies mechanistic interpretability and causal interventions to separate what the model represents from how it uses those representations. It also connects to broader industry debates about evaluation, safety, and whether scaling alone yields reliable internal models.
key_points: TaxiGPT actually learns useful internal structure: it represents intersections and streets, tracks its position, and uses a goal compass to guide navigation. Its apparent incoherence is not simply a missing world model.

The failures trace to interference between superposed intersection features. When multiple intersection representations overlap in the same activation space, localization within the internal map becomes disrupted, causing wrong turns or navigation errors.

Affordance packing helps reduce these errors by grouping intersections that share the same legal moves. This makes representations more robust to superposition interference and limits the downstream consequences of localization mistakes.

The authors propose mechanistic indicators to compare models and find that world-modeling capacities emerge at different stages of training. This suggests internal maps are not all-or-nothing but develop unevenly.
The paper argues for a shift from asking whether a model has a world model to mechanistically studying its world modeling: the interacting capacities that represent an environment and guide behavior.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this work reframes evaluation of agents and world models. Instead of judging only task success, labs can use mechanistic indicators and causal interventions to diagnose internal representations, feature interference, and training-stage emergence. For developers, it offers practical signals: build agents with disentangled or affordance-aware representations, and expect world modeling to develop gradually. It also supports safer deployment because failures can be predicted and mitigated rather than treated as mysterious. For regular users, the near-term effect may be more reliable navigation, planning, and embodied assistants, but also a reminder that fluent behavior does not guarantee a coherent internal map.
report.tools: Readers can explore mechanistic interpretability with TransformerLens, nnsight, and SAELens for activation patching and sparse autoencoders; Captum and PyTorch for causal interventions; CircuitsVis and Neuroscope for visualizing attention and neurons. ARENA exercises and Neel Nanda's interpretability resources offer practical tutorials. For world-model evaluation, watch agent benchmarks such as MiniGrid, Crafter, and NetHack, plus open-source RL environments like Gymnasium.
